releases.title: Image fields created before 0.45 keep their picture again

changes.text: Resource tables built before 0.45.0 still stored image and file fields as a BIGINT media id, so the JSON value written since then was coerced into the integer column — silently to 0 outside strict mode — and every saved entry lost its image right after the preview appeared. Those columns are now widened to JSON on the first request after the update, which keeps the stored ids readable; the only way out before was a schema re-publish behind the destructive-migration confirmation

Field names and image size prefixes are transliterated to snake_case identifiers as you type, so a Cyrillic look-alike character can no longer produce a name the backend rejects; when it still does, the error quotes the raw value instead of only the pattern

releases.title: Shared form controls, Lottie-free empty states and correct image rotation

changes.text: Baking a 90° or 270° rotation turned the image the wrong way: GD's imagerotate counts counter-clockwise, so the clockwise angles from the editor were negated twice. Rotation is now covered by a test that checks where the pixels land

Transparency survives a transform again: the alpha helper no longer paints over an image that already holds pixels, the transparent fill covers the full canvas instead of stopping one pixel short, and a missing gd extension reports itself instead of failing with an undefined function
Select, Textarea and Alert components plus a shared control stylesheet (control.ts), so every form control in the admin panel gets the same height, border, focus ring and disabled state

Native selects and textareas across schema builder, entries, resource settings, custom APIs, API playground, webhooks, integrations, tokens, users and API access were replaced with those components, dropping a dozen copies of hand-written control classes
Empty states are compact info alerts instead of a Lottie animation, which removes the @lottiefiles/dotlottie-react dependency and its 235 KB animation payload from the admin bundle

An upload whose variants cannot be generated no longer fails the whole request: the original keeps its media id, the field gets filled and the picker explains why the sizes are missing, instead of leaving an orphaned file in the library

Re-saving an entry keeps its image variants: the variant map now also reads the shape the admin panel sends back, not only the stored prefix-to-id form, and variant generation lifts the time limit so a long list of sizes cannot abort halfway

Requests that answer with HTML instead of JSON — PHP fatals, nginx 413 or 504, proxy error pages — are reported with their status and a readable excerpt instead of a JSON syntax error, and an error envelope returned with HTTP 200 is no longer treated as success

releases.title: Update screen finally shows what is about to arrive

changes.text: The update preview was always empty and the breaking-change gate could never trigger: notes were read from the local changelog.json, which only goes up to the installed version. They now come from the release manifest, which carries the last 25 releases, with the local file as fallback

latest.json is generated by scripts/latest-json.php from changelog.json instead of a hardcoded empty changelog, and the release build fails when changelog.json has no entry for the version being shipped

releases.title: Interactive image crop editor and shareable entry links

changes.text: Every image in an image field now has an edit button that opens a crop editor: drag to reposition, scroll or use the slider to zoom, rotate in 90° steps and flip horizontally or vertically

The editor has one tab per size from the schema, so a single size can get its own framing while the rest keep following the base crop; tabs show a dot when a size is overridden and an amber dot when the selected crop is smaller than the target and would be upscaled

Crop editor extras: live previews of every size that update while dragging, a rule-of-thirds grid, keyboard control (arrows to pan, Shift for bigger steps, +/− to zoom, [ ] to rotate, 0 to reset) and buttons to reset size framing or all edits at once

POST /admin/api/media/{id}/edit bakes rotation, flips and a crop rect into a new master image and regenerates every variant from it; the original upload is kept and linked through the new cms_media.source_id column, so reopening the editor always starts from full quality instead of re-cropping an already cropped file
Image field values carry sourceId, edit and overrides alongside the existing id, rotation, positions and variants; resource package export/import remaps the source id too

Entry editing lives at /resources/:id/data/:entryId, so an open entry card can be linked, bookmarked, opened in a new tab or reached with the browser's back button; the card has a copy-link button and the entries table edit action is now a real link
scripts/seed-demo.php fails with a clear message when a media upload returns no id instead of silently seeding entries with media id 0

releases.title: Fix the broken 0.45.3 autoloader and make updates recoverable

changes.text: 0.45.3 shipped a Composer autoloader generated two levels below the project root, so every Cms\* class resolved outside the install and any request died with an empty HTTP 500; the release build now installs Composer inside the staged tree and refuses to zip a tree that cannot boot
Cms\* classes load through a built-in PSR-4 autoloader in src/autoload.php, so a broken or missing vendor/ can no longer take the site down — the project has no runtime Composer dependencies

Updates are staged and swapped instead of overwritten in place: preflight checks (PHP version, write permissions, disk space) run before anything changes, the release is unpacked to storage/update-work-<version> and verified, then directories are moved in with rename() and a journal that can undo the swap

An update whose worker was killed mid-swap (PHP-FPM request_terminate_timeout ignores set_time_limit(0)) is rolled back automatically on the next request, and the pre-update backup now also covers vendor/, install.php, scripts/ and the public entry points

scripts/restore.php recovers a broken install without Composer, the database or any CMS class: diagnose, fix-autoload, restore from backup, reinstall a release, unlock a stuck update — from the CLI or from the browser with a token
scripts/verify-tree.php reports whether an install or a staged release can boot, and fatal errors are now recorded in storage/logs/php-fatal.log instead of vanishing behind an empty 500
Release zips are built from a clean HEAD checkout and no longer carry frontend sources, tests or CI config, so an update touches far fewer files
